# 17 Bass Patterns That Changed My Life — timestamped study notes

**Source:** [Production Music Live video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0gKJ3pgIqI0), published 27 September 2026; **title:** *17 Bass Patterns That Changed My Life (+ Sound Design)*. Presenter: Leo (as identified in the video). Runtime ~41:14.

**Source status (checked 1 November 2026):** The full English auto-generated YouTube captions were accessible through the connected browser's YouTube tab and reviewed. This document is an **original paraphrased study guide, not a verbatim transcript**. Auto-captions contain errors (notably 'baseline' for 'bassline' and 'Frigen' for 'Phrygian'). Musical details visible in the piano roll are not necessarily recoverable exactly from captions; do not treat these descriptions as definitive note-for-note MIDI transcriptions.

**Related primary source:** [Production Music Live's companion article](https://www.productionmusiclive.com/blogs/news/bassline-patterns), 28 September 2026, offers a shorter discussion of six recurring techniques.

## Chapters and the 17 approaches

Video chapters are linked to their stated starting times. The notes combine the chapter headings with the corresponding numbered examples in the narration.

| # | Video | Approach | Practical takeaway (paraphrased) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [0:38 Groovy](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0gKJ3pgIqI0&t=38s) | Brunello-style groove | A-minor riff, shifting note positions across a sixteenth grid and varying durations; toms and percussion complete the pulse. Sustained/saw-based timbre. |
| 2 | [3:07 Indie Dance](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0gKJ3pgIqI0&t=187s) | Playful/plucky indie-dance bass | Short notes and offbeat accents; G-minor context, root/fifth/seventh colours; saw-based pluck with distortion and sidechain. |
| 3 | [5:44 Deep House](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0gKJ3pgIqI0&t=344s) | Melodic/deep layered bass | Rhythmic sixteenth placements, more than one bass part, character/wide layers and a supporting low foundation; treat parts as an arrangement. |
| 4 | [9:22 Sustained](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0gKJ3pgIqI0&t=562s) | Sustained melodic-house foundation | Simpler long notes and scale-degree motion; Dorian-like hopeful colour discussed; melodies carry much of the interest. Gentle pitch bend can connect notes. |
| 5 | [11:27 Octave Jumps](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0gKJ3pgIqI0&t=687s) | Octave accent pattern | Mix note lengths and shifted sixteenths with occasional higher notes. Multiple tonal layers and active percussion support the groove. |
| 6 | [14:24 Driving](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0gKJ3pgIqI0&t=864s) | Driving progressive-house interlock | Two bass parts split the rhythmic work; one establishes the low pattern while another fills/answers selected spaces. |
| 7 | [16:20 Progressive](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0gKJ3pgIqI0&t=980s) | Multilayer progressive bass | Low foundation plus midrange character and delay-based motion. Contrasting layers are more expressive than one very busy MIDI part. |
| 8 | [19:09 Bouncy](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0gKJ3pgIqI0&t=1149s) | Bouncy bass | Repeated hits interact with kick placement; oscillators/harmonic character and articulation can create bounce without a complicated melody. |
| 9 | [20:47 Gnarly](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0gKJ3pgIqI0&t=1247s) | Dark/gnarly bass | Phrygian colour and off-grid sixteenths create tension and movement; separate low fundamentals from aggressive midrange harmonics. |
| 10 | [23:38 Organic](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0gKJ3pgIqI0&t=1418s) | Organic / band-like eighth-note bass | Simple, almost played-in eighth-note foundation; the melody and percussion contribute the larger expression; saw pluck resembles a played instrument. |
| 11 | [25:23 Classic](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0gKJ3pgIqI0&t=1523s) | Classic tech-house bass | Mix third/fourth sixteenth placements, with sub and mid parts; quick pitch-decay can make the bass transient resemble an extra kick. |
| 12 | [27:13 Dark](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0gKJ3pgIqI0&t=1633s) | Dark tech-house bass | Phrygian tension, rhythmic variation between sixteenth positions 2/4/3, layered sub and resonant/acid-like mid-bass. Change melodic details between drops. |
| 13 | [29:34 Movement](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0gKJ3pgIqI0&t=1774s) | Long-and-short sustained bass | Combine long notes with rhythmic gaps and varied scale degrees; Phrygian is used for darker colour; leave tiny breaks between notes to preserve articulation. |
| 14 | [32:01 Rolling](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0gKJ3pgIqI0&t=1921s) | Rolling + groovy + impact | Distinct parts supply sub foundation, repeated/rolling motion and a brief drop impact; parts need not all carry the same rhythm. |
| 15 | [33:36 Afro Tech](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0gKJ3pgIqI0&t=2016s) | Layered Afro-tech groove | Syncopated sixteenths, differentiated sub/mid rhythms, and occasional gliding drop notes; contrasting parts create movement. |
| 16 | [35:58 Deep](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0gKJ3pgIqI0&t=2158s) | Deep Afro-influenced layers | Some upper sounds appear only in the gaps of the main bass, with glide and drone textures; percussion helps them act as one rhythmic phrase. |
| 17 | [37:54 Call & Response](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0gKJ3pgIqI0&t=2274s) | Tech-house question-and-answer | A grounded low bass 'calls', an upper/midrange line answers, and percussion supplies movement in the rests. Phrygian colour and distinct sound layers support the exchange. |

## Six recurrent lessons confirmed by the creator's article

1. **Separate sub from mid character.** A comparatively simple sine-derived sub preserves low-end stability while a harmonically richer mid layer supplies motion. The article suggests different sidechain amounts for each.
2. **Use sixteenth positions strategically.** Placing selected attacks on subdivisions 2 and 4 instead of every downbeat changes the relationship with the kick.
3. **Vary articulation and register.** Short stabs, two-sixteenth holds and occasional octave accents help phrases feel intentional.
4. **Compose with gaps.** A phrase, a rest and a response can work better than continuously sounding bass notes.
5. **Choose scale colour deliberately.** Major, minor and Phrygian give different moods; Phrygian's flattened second adds immediate tension above the tonic.
6. **Build attack without simply increasing volume.** Modest additional harmonics and a short downward pitch envelope can create perceived punch.

These six items paraphrase the [PML article](https://www.productionmusiclive.com/blogs/news/bassline-patterns); specific Serum 2 settings are available there.

## Ableton Move application — original exercise, not transcribed MIDI

Move's four-track constraint makes **arrangement decisions** especially important.

- **Track 1 drums:** kick, hats, toms and percussion on one Drum track.
- **Track 2 bass:** start with one bass sound and a two-bar MIDI hook. Explore the sixteenth placements before adjusting timbre.
- **Track 3 chord/lead:** provide harmonic context or the answering phrase.
- **Track 4 optional:** additional texture, hook, or a separate mid-bass response if the first bass sound does not carry enough character.

**Experiment:** at 124 BPM with an A-minor bass patch, place short A1 notes at sixteenth steps 4, 7, 12 and 15 against four-to-the-floor kicks on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13. Compare this with moving bass hits onto the kicks. Adjust one note's length or replace one with A2. This is an independently invented exercise, **not** a claim that these are the video's MIDI notes.

## In Live 12 Suite

Split a simple bass into sub and mid layers if the arrangement needs it; keep low-end energy controlled, audition sidechain in the full drum mix, compare different MIDI onset positions at 1/16 resolution, and try a pitch envelope on the bass attack. Check that overlapping lows do not sum unpredictably. Preserve contrast between groove layers and use clip variations rather than constant note density.
